headline: The build-out now runs on outside money, and Treasuries are charging for it
verdict: Hyperscaler capex is still accelerating: $181.5bn in 2026Q2, +86.5% YoY, and 82% of operating cash flow on a trailing basis, up from 40% in 2024Q1. The gap is being filled with bonds and equity, yet IG spreads have barely moved (IG OAS 0.79%, +4bp on the year); the cost is showing up in rates, with the 10y at 5.11% after the Fed's September 16 hike. This week the market kept splitting spenders by whether they show product revenue: Meta +13.0%, Oracle -6.6%.
what_changed: The 10y Treasury rose 10bp on the week to 5.11% and the 2y 11bp to 4.85%, extending the move that followed the Fed's September 16 hike to 3.75–4.00%.
CoreWeave priced an upsized $3.7bn 2.875% convertible due 2033 on September 18, up from a $3.0bn launch, with a $0.5bn upsize option.
Meta rose 13.0% on the week after Wells Fargo raised its target on early adoption of the Muse AI agent: a spender being paid for product revenue.
Oracle fell 6.6% on the week and is down 52.1% over a year, two weeks after reporting negative free cash flow alongside $664bn of backlog.
Semis kept pulling away: SMH/SPY rose to 159.9 from 147.9 a month ago, while the equal-weight S&P fell to 97.0 from 102.6 against SPY.

spend.claim: Capex is still accelerating, and 2026 guidance points higher again.
spend.body: No new guidance this week. Combined capex was $181.5bn in 2026Q2, +86.5% YoY, and $566.4bn over four quarters. The 2026 guides add to $720–745bn: Alphabet $195–205bn, Amazon $220bn, Meta $130–145bn, Microsoft about $175bn. Oracle guides $90–95bn for its fiscal year to May 2027. Some of the growth is price, not volume: Amazon tied its $20bn raise to memory costs. Microsoft's lower figure reflects moving data-center leases to operating leases, not less spending.

evidence.text: Alphabet raised its 2026 capex guide to $195–205bn (July 22)
Amazon raised 2026 capex to $220bn, citing memory prices
Meta Q2 release: 2026 capex $130–145bn incl. finance lease principal
Microsoft: CY2026 capex about $175bn after lease accounting change
Oracle FY27 capex guide $90–95bn, net cash capex under $70bn

funding.claim: The spenders now fund the gap in the bond and equity markets, and the price is showing up in Treasuries, not IG spreads.
funding.body: Trailing capex is 82% of operating cash flow, and combined long-term debt rose from $212.5bn in 2024Q4 to $464.1bn in 2026Q2. Alphabet sold $84.75bn of equity in June; Oracle raised $20bn through an at-the-market program. IG OAS is 0.79%, only +4bp on the year, but the 10y is +99bp and the term premium +50bp. Hyperscaler paper is cheapening at the margin: 2026 new-issue concessions averaged 12bp against 2.25bp in 2025. This week CoreWeave priced a $3.7bn convertible.

evidence.text: Alphabet priced an $84.75bn equity raise for AI infrastructure (June 3)
Oracle completed a $20bn at-the-market equity issuance in fiscal Q1 (June–August)
Hyperscaler new-issue concessions 12bp in 2026 vs 2.25bp in 2025; cover ratios below 2x (July 29)
FOMC raises the target range to 3.75–4.00% (September 16)

receivers.claim: Suppliers are booking the money, and their growth is still speeding up.
receivers.body: No new supplier results this week. NVDA revenue was $96.2bn in 2026Q2, +105.9% YoY, and it guides about $108bn for the next quarter. Broadcom grew +85.5% and Micron +345.7% in their latest quarters, the latter as much memory pricing as volume. TSMC's August sales rose 53.3% YoY. Vertiv, the power-and-cooling proxy, is steadier at +24.1%. Micron reports its fiscal Q4 on September 30, the next read on memory pricing.

evidence.text: NVIDIA Q2 FY27: $96.2bn revenue, Q3 outlook about $108.0bn
Micron reports fiscal Q4 on September 30, 2026

macro.claim: IT investment is carrying about a third of GDP growth, while productivity has cooled.
macro.body: No new GDP or productivity data this week. Over the last four quarters, IT equipment plus software contributed 0.70pp of 2.12% average real GDP growth, or 33%. Productivity growth slowed to +2.2% over four quarters from +2.9% a quarter earlier. Electricity CPI is +4.0% YoY, down from +6.8% three months ago. The inflation behind the Fed's hike came from energy, with gasoline +27.4% YoY in August, not from power prices.

evidence.text: BLS August CPI: headline +3.4%, core +2.4%, gasoline +27.4% YoY

market.claim: The market pays suppliers and spenders that show revenue, and punishes spenders that only show capex.
market.body: Over a year, SMH relative to SPY is at 159.9 while the equal-weight hyperscaler basket is at 81.5. Within the spenders, Meta rose 13.0% this week on early adoption of its paid Muse agent; Oracle fell 6.6% and is down 52.1% on the year. Utilities are at 80.1 relative to SPY, down from 88.6 a month ago, trading as rate-sensitive bond proxies rather than AI winners. Breadth narrowed: RSP/SPY fell to 97.0 from 102.6.

evidence.text: Meta jumps after Wells Fargo target raise on Muse AI agent adoption (September 21)

tripwires.name: Spend slows
tripwires.reading: Combined capex +86.5% YoY in 2026Q2 (data/summary.md); no guidance cuts, three of four raised in July.

tripwires.name: Cash burn
tripwires.reading: T4Q capex/OCF 82% in 2026Q2, up from 75% a quarter earlier; 100% is the line (data/summary.md).

tripwires.name: IG spreads wake up
tripwires.reading: IG OAS 0.79%, BBB OAS 0.97% on 2026-09-24, against 1.10% / 1.30% (FRED).

tripwires.name: Weak link cracks
tripwires.reading: Oracle is BBB- at S&P since July 9, one notch above high yield; CoreWeave is still raising, $3.7bn convertible on September 18.

tripwires.name: Suppliers roll over
tripwires.reading: NVDA revenue +105.9% YoY, guiding about $108bn next quarter; Micron reports September 30.

tripwires.name: Rates bite
tripwires.reading: 10y 5.11% on 2026-09-23, +41bp in a month, against 5.50%; term premium 0.96% against 1.25% (FRED).

tripwires.name: Payoff shows up (bullish)
tripwires.reading: Productivity +2.2% over four quarters, down from +2.9%; not two quarters above 2.5%.

thesis_suggestions: Point 6: the funding cost is showing up in Treasury yields and term premium, not in IG spreads, which are +4bp on the year. Consider saying so and treating T6 (rates) as the main funding tripwire, with T3 (spreads) as confirmation.
Point 5: the split is not simply suppliers vs spenders. Meta's week says spenders get paid when they show product revenue. Consider framing it as 'the market pays for monetization, not for capex'.
